# Cross-Device Context-Scaling Comparison: A76 vs A57

## Throughput: A76 (RK3588) vs A57 (Jetson Nano)

| Config | A76 ctx=1 | A76 ctx=4096 | A57 ctx=1 | A57 ctx=4096 | A76 slowdown | A57 slowdown |
|--------|----------:|-------------:|----------:|-------------:|-------------:|-------------:|
| 0.8B INT8 hybrid | 10.70 | 5.01 | 2.95 | 1.67 | 2.14× | 1.77× |
| 0.8B INT8 pure-GDN | 10.46 | 10.44 | 2.88 | 2.89 | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| 4B INT8 hybrid | 1.84 | 1.19 | 0.57 | 0.42 | 1.55× | 1.36× |
| 4B INT8 pure-GDN | 1.84 | 1.83 | 0.57 | 0.59 | 1.01× | 0.97× |
| 0.8B FP32 hybrid | 7.97 | 4.31 | 2.25 | 1.18 | 1.85× | 1.91× |
| 4B FP32 hybrid | 1.04 | 0.79 | 0.43 | 0.33 | 1.32× | 1.30× |

## Key insight: GDN advantage scales with context on every device

Both A76 and A57 show the same pattern: hybrid throughput degrades at long context (1.3–2.1× slowdown from ctx=1 to ctx=4096), while pure-GDN stays flat (<1% variance). The GDN advantage — constant-time decode regardless of conversation length — holds across Arm core classes.
